phase: P09 (loyalty: accounts, points ledger, programs, HTTP access)
scope: modules/loyalty domain entities, value objects and repositories
infra http routes, controller and validation schemas
checkout loyalty redemption path (P06-04) re-checked against the new persistence
reviewed_without_change: Program management (create/update/delete) is admin-only and was confirmed correct.
Purchase earning is idempotent per order (existing EARN entry check) and runs after checkout commit.
Checkout redemption (P06-04) goes through the same service, so it gains the atomic persistence and the balance constraint.

findings.problem: Account balances were read, changed in memory and written back as absolute values, so concurrent earning and redeeming overwrote each other: four simultaneous redemptions of 60 on a 100-point balance all succeeded, and five of six simultaneous earnings were lost.
findings.change: The repository persists the change since the account was read as atomic increments; a database CHECK (current_balance >= 0) refuses a redemption that concurrent activity has made impossible, reported as insufficient points. The constraint is added NOT VALID and validated with a warning instead of failing on historical data.
findings.verification: Integration LoyaltyPointsConcurrency on PostgreSQL: baseline 4 of 4 redemptions succeeded and the balance stayed at 110 after 6 earnings; fixed exactly 1 redemption succeeds (balance 40) and all changes add up.

findings.problem: The account and its ledger entry were written in separate statements, so a failure between them changed a balance without a record (or the reverse), and balanceAfter was the in-memory value, wrong under concurrency (six entries all recorded 110).
findings.change: Earning, redeeming and adjusting write the account and the ledger entry in one database transaction, and balanceAfter is the balance the database holds after that change.
findings.verification: Integration: six concurrent earnings record balances 110..160 in sequence; a refused redemption writes no ledger entry.

findings.problem: GET /loyalty/account took the user id from the query, so any customer could read (and create) another customer's points account, and GET /loyalty/transactions returned any account's or order's history.
findings.change: Customers always get their own account and only their own account's transactions; staff can still look up any customer.
findings.verification: E2E: baseline returned the other customer's account; fixed returns the caller's own account and staff lookups still work.

findings.problem: POST /loyalty/points/redeem was open to any signed-in user with the user id taken from the body, so anyone could burn another customer's points; awarding points was allowed for the read-only ANALYST role.
findings.change: Direct redeem and award are limited to admins and customer service; customers spend points at checkout, where the server applies the redemption (P06-04).
findings.verification: E2E: baseline customer redemption of another customer's points returned 201; fixed 403. Lifecycle test now redeems as customer service.

findings.problem: Manual adjustments recorded createdBy from the request body, so the audit trail could name any user.
findings.change: Adjustments are attributed to the signed-in admin; the body field is optional and ignored. API client regenerated.
findings.verification: E2E: baseline stored the forged id; fixed stores the admin's id.

tests.new: integration LoyaltyPointsConcurrency (4), E2E loyalty Account ownership (3)
tests.baseline: All 6 new concurrency and ownership cases failed against the previous code (stash baseline).
tests.database_suites: All E2E and integration suites: 152 tests in 45 files pass
tests.final: 1526 unit tests in 119 files; root/tooling tsc; 7/7 workspace type-checks; loyalty ESLint; API client regenerated and drift check passes; migration applies and schema drift check passes

follow_ups: Two simultaneous first requests for a new member can both try to create the account; the second fails on the unique user id instead of reusing the account.

Point expiry (expirePoints) is not called anywhere; as written it would expire the same earned entries on every run and ignore points already spent, so it needs a design decision (and its own transaction) before it is enabled.
Tier is still written as an absolute value; concurrent changes can only leave it one step behind until the next activity.
